Allright I am looking to create a agent trace viewer, these data is available in hugging face. But none of the data viewer works.
The tool should be able to work locally and on aws instance. 
The data can be downloaded to S3 or on local disk. 

Here is my short requirements.

The goal is to following.
It must take one or multiple hf repo URL. This can be driven via simple YAML config. 
Would allow me to explore the dataset. I see descriptions in the web but best to have this from the data directly.
It needs to allow me to search for sesssions that I am interested? How do I run the search, how would I know what to search for?
Lets create a CLI tool first. The 2nd step is to create  a web front end. We would very likely run that tool in an aws instance.
Questions:
Do we need to download the parquet file. In case of aws downloading in S3 makes sense. Localy also it an make sense. 
If there is an option to browse the data without downloading first, it is preferrable. Make it option so users can be explicit.
Use python, already installed the codebase is majority python. Unless it is better to use another language and library because it is fast, compact etc.
The folder where you will work is trace_utils

Lets brainstorm first

questions.question: What should "search" cover in the v1 CLI? (This drives whether we build a full-text index or just structured filters.)

options.label: Full-text over content
options.description: Find sessions whose prompts/responses mention a term or regex, e.g. 'sessions about playwright' or 'mentions kubernetes'. Uses DuckDB FTS / regex over message text.

options.label: Structured metadata filters
options.description: Filter by fields: vendor, model, date range, gitBranch, #turns, tools used, token/cost if present. e.g. --vendor codex --min-turns 20.

options.label: Guided discovery first
options.description: An 'explore/describe' command that profiles a dataset (fields, value distributions, top tools, token ranges, sample prompts) so you learn what's searchable before searching.

options.label: Semantic / embedding search
options.description: Vector search over message content for meaning-based similarity. Heavier: needs an embedding model + vector store. Likely defer past v1.

questions.question: Across the 3 (differently-shaped) datasets, should v1 present each dataset in its own discovered field paths, or map them into one unified session/event schema?

options.label: Dataset-native (Recommended)
options.description: Discovery/filters/search operate on each dataset's own discovered field paths. No forced common schema. Matches 'show me what's actually in THIS data'. A thin common view (session_id, vendor, timestamp, text) is best-effort on top. Simpler, honest, ships faster.

options.label: Unified normalized schema
options.description: Build adapters that map every dataset into one canonical session/event model, so the same query works everywhere. More powerful cross-dataset queries, but requires per-dataset mapping code and hides the raw shape — more work, more assumptions, slower to v1.
